claims: Authority is modeled as an explicit rank: advisory < stage < execute.
An allowed execute-class request must be a live-execution request.
Any allowed live-execution request requires a capability whose liveExecutionAllowed flag is true.
A non-live advisory capability cannot authorize execute-class or live-execution requests.
Allowed delegated actions respect their declared loss ceiling.
A zero-loss capability cannot authorize positive requested loss.
When composed with the poka-yoke submit gate, advisory non-live authority and submitAllowed cannot jointly authorize execute/live requests.
Dangerous requests without the interlock are blocked at both the capability boundary and the submit-interlock boundary.
proof_method: composition with the existing poka-yoke submit theorem

checker_commands.command: cd lean-mathlib && lake build Proofs.AgentCapabilityBounds Proofs.AdvisoryPokayokeBridge

checker_commands.result: passed with pre-existing linter warnings in unrelated proof files

boundaries: This is a proof-level authority model. Runtime systems still need to map concrete KRR/autotrader/API capabilities into these fields.
The theorem prevents advisory non-live authority from authorizing execute/live requests; it does not prove that every deployed integration uses this capability model.
The loss ceiling is an integer field in the model and assumes the caller supplies a faithful requestedLoss value.
The poka-yoke bridge relies on the existing submitAllowed and dangerous_without_interlock_blocks definitions.
